capital: The largest pile of people in the realm, and they all know it.
Where the laws are written, ignored, and then written again, angrier.
town: A market, a temple, and a grudge that goes back four generations.
Prosperous enough for two taverns, which is two too many for the priest.
Everyone here is related. Nobody will say how.
village: Eleven houses and a well that everyone is politely lying about.
The kind of place that has one road and uses it mostly for leaving.
A hamlet with a scarecrow the locals nod to.
castle: Fortified against an enemy that stopped existing a century ago.
Somebody's ancestral seat. Somebody's, anyway. It changes hands often.
dungeon: The stairs go down further than the hill is tall. Nobody wants to discuss this.
Sealed by royal decree. The seal is on the inside.
Three expeditions went in. Two came out. Neither of them was the second one.
cave: A hole. A committed, ambitious hole.
Something is breathing in there, and it is doing it on purpose.
The local children dare each other to the entrance and no further.
ruin: Stones arranged by people who had better tools than you and still lost.
The architecture is beautiful. The reason it is empty is not.
Somebody put a great deal of work into this and then something happened.
tower: One room per floor. Each floor is worse than the one below it.
Built by a wizard with something to prove and no planning permission.
It is taller on the inside. That is not a metaphor.
shrine: A god nobody remembers, still accepting offerings out of habit.
The altar is cracked and the crack is the important part.
Pilgrims come here to ask for things. The answers are technically yes.
camp: Tents, a fire, and a very specific silence when strangers arrive.
Somebody is cooking. Somebody is always cooking. Nobody is eating.
oddity: There is no good word for what is going on here.
A door standing in a field, hinged to nothing, firmly shut.
The grass grows in a perfect circle and the birds route around it.
Lit, at night, by nothing anybody will admit to.
The locals have built a fence around it and a shrine facing away from it.
Everything here is the wrong century and none of it will discuss that.

dungeon: They say the bottom floor is furnished. Furnished, mind. Curtains and everything.
A fellow went in with forty men and came out with a very good soup recipe.
ruin: My grandmother's grandmother saw the lights there. She said they waved.
Take nothing from a ruin. Or take everything. Half measures are what get you.
tower: The wizard's still up there. Been up there since before the war. Not once come down.
Knock three times and it opens. Knock four and you're the one who answers.
oddity: Don't go. Don't. I'm not going to explain, because I can't.
It moved last spring. Two fields east. Nobody talks about it at market.

hitFlavor: {A} {V} {T} — {D}. That will bruise in a shape.
{T} takes {D} and does not enjoy it.
{A} {V} {T} for {D}. Somewhere, a bard is already lying about this.
critFlavor: {A} {V} {T} for an unreasonable {D}. Everyone present feels it.
{D}. {T} was not built for that and now demonstrably is not.
{A} {V} {T} for {D}. That was the good one.
A perfect {V}. {D} damage. {T} briefly leaves the ground.
missFlavor: {A} swings at {T} and hits the concept of air.
{A} misses {T} entirely and has to live with that.
{T} is simply not where {A} committed to.
{A} whiffs. {T} does not even do it the courtesy of dodging.
deathFlavor: {T} falls over and stays that way.
{T} goes down without ceremony, which is the only dignified way to do it.
{T} is defeated, and looks faintly relieved about it.
levelFlavor: Level {L}. You feel marginally harder to kill.
Level {L}. Something in your back stops hurting and something else starts.
Level {L}. You have gotten better at this, which is a worrying sentence.
Level {L}. The universe files an updated assessment of you.
idleFlavor: The wind carries something that is nearly a voice.
A crow watches you from a fence post and takes notes.
Somewhere behind you, something decides not to.
The road goes on. It is not in a hurry and neither, apparently, are you.
You smell rain, or a fire, or a very confident animal.
For a moment the whole world sounds like it is holding its breath.
npcLine: "You want my advice? Don't go east. Or do. I'm not your mother."
"They found another one in the well. Same as the last. Same exactly."
"I'd sell you something, but you've got the look of a person who haggles."
"My husband went into the woods for firewood. That was in spring. We have plenty of firewood."
"Don't trust the priest. Don't trust the miller. Trust the goat."
"Everyone says adventurer like it's a job. It's a diagnosis."
"I've seen four of you this month. I've seen one of you come back."
"There's coin in monster parts, if you're not squeamish and not particular."
"You'll want a better sword. You'll want a better everything, frankly."
"Ask me about the tower. Go on. Ask me. ...No, I've changed my mind."
"My cousin was eaten by something with opinions. He'd have hated that."
"Gods are real, they're just not very good at their jobs."
"If a door in a field is shut, friend, leave it shut."
signText: NO ENTRY. THIS MEANS YOU. YES, YOU SPECIFICALLY.
Beware of the dog. The dog is fine. Beware of what the dog is afraid of.
Lost: one sword, sentimental value, answers to 'Gerald'.
By order of the Crown, this place does not exist. Please do not tell it.
Free to a good home. Or any home. Please.
Trespassers will be prosecuted. Survivors will be prosecuted twice.
The bridge toll is one coin or one secret. Exact change appreciated.
Here lies nobody. We checked. Twice.
Do not read the next sign.

ask: "I need {N} {I}. Don't ask what for. Actually do ask, later, when I've had a drink."
"Bring me {N} {I} and I'll make it worth your while. Modestly worth. Let's not oversell it."
"{N} {I}. That's the order. My supplier was eaten, which is the third time this year."
nag: "Still {N} {I}. The number has not changed. I would have mentioned."
"{I}. {N} of them. I'm not going anywhere, worse luck."
thank: "All {N}. You actually did it. I had a whole speech ready for if you didn't."
"Lovely. Don't tell me where you got them. I mean it. Don't."

ask: "There's {M} out there. {N} of them, ideally fewer by supper."
"Kill {N} {M}. I'd do it myself but I've got a bad back and a good excuse."
"{N} {M}. They've been at the livestock, the washing, and once at my aunt."
nag: "{M}. {N} of them. They are not culling themselves, which we tried."
"Still out there, then. The {M}. I can hear them from here."
thank: "That's the {M} dealt with. The village will be insufferable about it for weeks."
"Done? Properly done? Right. I'll stop flinching at noises."

ask: "Somebody needs to go into {P} and put a stop to whatever is in there."
"{P}. Nobody's come back from it. That's not a warning, that's a job opening."
"Clear out {P}. My brother went in. I'd like the place emptied and, if convenient, him back."
nag: "{P} is still there. Still full. Still nobody's problem but yours, apparently."
"Have you been to {P} yet? No? It hasn't improved."
thank: "{P} is quiet. First time in years. Feels wrong, honestly."
"You went in and came out. That puts you ahead of everyone else who tried."

ask: "Take this to {P}. Don't open it. Don't shake it. Don't listen to it."
"A parcel for {P}. It's paid for. It's mostly legal. It's definitely paid for."
"Get this to {P} before it goes off. I won't define 'off'."
nag: "{P}. The parcel. It is not improving in your bag."
thank: "It arrived. Nobody's shouting. That's the best outcome I'd planned for."
"Delivered, and you didn't open it. I can tell. You'd be different if you had."

recruitPitch: "You're going out there. I can tell. You've got the walk of someone who hasn't been told no recently."
"I fight for money. I've tried the other reasons. Money is the one that works."
"Last three employers didn't come back. I did. Draw your own conclusions about who to hire."
"I'm cheap, I'm rested, and I have absolutely nothing else on."
"I can hold a sword, hold a grudge, and hold my tongue. Two of those come free."
"You look like you need someone standing between you and the horizon."
"I'm between wars. It's a seasonal trade."
"My last party voted me out. There were only two of us. I'd like that on the record."
"I don't ask where we're going. I've found that helps."
"Take me with you. This town has one well and I've read all of it."
recruitJoin: {N} counts it twice, pockets it, and falls in behind you without another word.
{N} shoulders their pack. "Right. Don't make this weird."
{N} takes the coin, looks at the road, and visibly reconsiders. Then follows anyway.
{N} shakes your hand for slightly too long and joins the company.
{N} says "you won't regret this" in the tone of someone who knows you will.
{N} is now your problem, and you are now theirs.
recruitLeave: {N} takes their share, says nothing, and walks off in a direction you did not choose.
{N} nods once. "No hard feelings. There were some. They're gone now."
{N} leaves the company, and takes the good waterskin.
{N} departs, already telling the story a different way.
{N} shrugs and goes. You will hear about this from strangers.
allyDown: {N} goes down hard and stays down.
{N} sits down in the middle of it and declines to get up.
{N} takes one too many and folds like a bad argument.
{N} is out of the fight, and loudly out of it.
{N} drops. This was not in the arrangement, and they say so on the way down.
allyUp: {N} gets back up, humiliated but structurally sound.
{N} is helped upright and immediately claims they were pacing themselves.
{N} comes round, checks their purse first, and stands.
{N} is upright again, and has notes.

beast: "Yes. I know. It's the ears. Everyone starts with the ears."
"I'll smell it before you see it. That's the whole pitch, really."
"I shed. I'm cheap. Those two facts are related."
fey: "I can't lie to you, which people think is a limitation. It is not."
"Don't accept anything I offer you for free. I'm being polite by warning you."
"My mother's side is complicated and I'd rather not go into it on the street."
undead: "I don't need the bed at the inn. That should factor into your offer."
"Technically I'm still under contract to a previous employer. Technically he's dead."
"I don't sleep, I don't eat, and I don't scare. Two of those are savings for you."
demon: "There's an arrangement. It doesn't involve you. It could, but it doesn't."
"I work cheap because the alternative is going home."
"Don't sign anything I hand you and we'll get on famously."
ooze: "I take a lot of hitting. That's not a boast, it's just what I am."
"I'll need to travel behind the horse, not on it. Long story. Wet story."
"Don't put me near the good furniture and this'll work out."
aberrant: "Nobody's established what I am. Nobody's pressed. I'd keep it that way."
"I'm going to be some distance from you at all times. It's better for both of us."
"People find me difficult to look at directly. Monsters find it worse."

rescue: You wake up in {P}. {N} is going through your pockets, which is how you know you are not dead.
{N} carried you into {P} and paid somebody to argue with the situation. It worked. It was not free.
You come round on a table in {P}. {N} is explaining to a physician that you are worth the effort, and being unconvincing.
{N} dragged you the whole way to {P} without once suggesting it was easier to leave you. They mention this. Repeatedly.
You are alive, in {P}, and considerably poorer. {N} does not explain the order those happened in.
revived: {N} sits up, furious, and rejoins the fight mid-sentence.
{N} comes back with the look of somebody who has been interrupted.
{N} is upright again and taking it personally.
{N} returns to the proceedings, having missed nothing important.

poison: {N} has been envenomed, and is now on a schedule.
Something goes into {N} that was not on the menu.
{N} starts to sweat in a colour.
burn: {N} is on fire. This is not a metaphor.
Parts of {N} begin to smoke in an organised way.
weaken: {N} loses something out of the arms.
Whatever {N} had, they have less of it now.

rumoured: "They say there's someone out there doing all this. Sounds made up to me."
"Heard a story about a stranger and a very bad afternoon. Wasn't you, was it. No. Course not."
"Something's been happening out east. Nobody knows who. I like that about it."
"There's a name going round with no face on it. Best kind of name."
celebrated: "It IS you. My sister's going to be sick. Can I touch the sword?"
"We heard. We all heard. Somebody's written a song and it does not scan."
"Whatever you're buying, mention my name. It won't help, but mention it."
"Stand there. Just stand there a moment. Right. That's done, thank you."
recognised: "I know your face. I don't know why I know your face."
"You're that one. From the thing. That everyone's -- no? Nothing? Right."
"Saw you in the market. Saw you in the market again. You're around a lot."
"You've got the look of somebody important. Have you done anything?"
notorious: "I'd rather you didn't stand so close to the window."
"We've heard. We've all heard. Buy something or move along."
"My cousin says you're not welcome here. My cousin says a lot of things."
"Not looking for trouble. Just noting where the door is."

sign: OPEN 24 HOURS. It has been shut since before anyone here was born.
NO LOITERING. Six people are loitering under it.
LEVEL 3 PARKING. There are no levels and no parking.
YOUR CALL IS IMPORTANT TO US.
THIS UNIT IS MONITORED. Nobody has ever found out by whom.
PLEASE MIND THE GAP. There is no gap. There is a field.
NOW HIRING. The application box is full of rainwater and frogs.
EXIT. It points at a hedge.
person: The light comes on at dusk. We do not know who pays for it.
My grandfather hung his washing on it. Nobody minded.
You are not from here. You are looking at it.
It hums. You get used to the humming.
The priest blessed it twice and it made no difference either way.
We had a cow go under the barrier once. She was fine. Different, but fine.
Do not put your hand in the slot. That is all I will say about the slot.
It was here before the village. The village came to it.
machine: A tall box with a lit window and a slot. Things are visible inside it.
The box takes a coin, thinks about it, and gives you something cold.
There is a picture on the front of a person enjoying themselves enormously.
It says PLEASE MAKE A SELECTION in a script nobody in the realm writes.
trash: A metal drum with a hinged lid. Somebody has been through it already.
A bin. Not a chest, a bin. There is a difference and it is mostly smell.

alone: Travelling on your own. That's a choice. There's usually somebody outside the inn who'd rather not be.
No one with you? The ones waiting outside the inn take a cut. They also take a hit meant for you.
You want somebody at your back. Ask outside the inn. They're not proud.
Alone, is it. The ones who come back mostly didn't start that way.
hurt: You're leaking. There's a bed here and the landlord has seen worse walk in.
Sleep it off. The beds are bad. They are still beds.
You've the look of the last three who didn't stop at the inn.
flush: That purse is making a noise. The shop's right there and it does not judge.
Coin's no use to you dead, and there's a counter in this town happy to prove it.
Spend it. Whatever's out there won't be impressed by your savings.
idle: Half this town needs something doing. The other half is the something.
People here have problems. Ask around. Nobody's shy about it.
You look unoccupied. That's a condition somebody here will cure for you.
broke: Monster parts sell. Not for much. But they sell.
You could shift what you're carrying. Somebody always wants it. Nobody knows why.
